evidence.curator_note: GENERIC SCHEME, printed under the heading 'EE+'. Same cyclic onium (oxocarbenium) precursor as Eq 8.51, but here the ring is drawn explicitly as a HEXAGON: Y+ at the top vertex, single-bonded to one ring carbon and double-bonded to the neighbouring ring carbon that carries R. The arrow is again labelled 'i, i' (two charge-site/inductive cleavages). Products: the cross-conjugated onium CH2=Y+-C(R)=CH2 plus neutral ETHYLENE (drawn as a bare double bond, i.e. an alkene - contrast Eq 8.51, whose neutral is drawn as a closed ring). INSTANTIATION (F/B): Y=O, R=CH3, hexagon = the 2-methyl-oxocarbenium of tetrahydropyran, C6H11O+ m/z 99.0804, charge localised on the ring oxygen exactly where the book prints the '+'. Product ion CH2=O+-C(CH3)=CH2, C4H7O+ m/z 71.0491. Book draws 3 arc(s); moves <1,2,3> are ALL drawn and no implicit move is required - the three two-electron arcs form one closed cascade running the same way round the ring, so the bookkeeping closes exactly. Arc 1 (upper right, tail on the Y=C bond, head pointing at the right ring bond): the Y=C pi pair drops into the C(R)-C bond (maps 2-4). Arc 2 (bottom, head at the lower-left ring bond): the ring sigma bond it leaves (maps 4-5) becomes the new C=C of the expelled ethylene (maps 5-6). Arc 3 (left, tail on the left ring bond, head pointing up at the Y-C bond): that sigma pair (maps 6-7) becomes the new CH2=Y+ pi bond (maps 1-7). Net: two ring bonds (4-5 and 6-7) are cleaved and three bond orders rise, the charge staying on Y throughout.
